title: Intersecting a Pixel subset with a band breaks linked extraction and hides the marker
verified: The plan's band recipe (lines 488 and 515) is about the same dataset, and there it works: Pixel & band gives the band-restricted spectrum. The plan never says that AND-ed subsets work across linked data, so 'plan_incorrect' overstates the problem. The limitation itself is real and not documented. A Pixel & band AndState gives an all-NaN profile on a WCS-linked dataset. The Pixel crosshair marker also disappears once the subset is any AndState, even on the same dataset. Both apply to released 1.27.0 and to core-combined.
recommendation: State this limitation in the time-wavelength recipe and in WP4. When a WP4 preset adds band or scan filters, compute the band on the target dataset and keep the Pixel subset bare, or intersect after translating to the target's pixels. Test the marker and linked spectra with filters active.
evidence: My probe t/test_v2_band.py, on released core with glue-qt and on core-combined with qt-profile. Output: 'bare linked [660..710]', 'pt & band(b) linked [nan x6]', 'pt & band(a) same [nan 37. 38. nan nan nan]', 'marker bare True', 'marker anded False AndState'. Code in released core: data.py:1733-1735 (the SliceSubsetState fast path is taken only for a bare state), subset.py:1371-1373 (a non-aligned dataset returns broadcast False), viewers/image/layer_artist.py:319-331 (the marker draws only for isinstance PixelSubsetState).

title: The fixed-layout tab registry does not work with app.viewers and is not restored from sessions
verified: This is confirmed and slightly worse than reported. A plain QWidget, as in the docs example, cannot even be added: add_fixed_layout_tab connects tab.subWindowActivated and raises AttributeError. A widget that defines that signal is added, but app.viewers then fails (it is reported as a missing attribute) and _update_viewer_in_focus raises on activeSubWindow. With a subWindowList shim the session saves, but restore rebuilds only GlueMdiArea tabs, so the fixed layout is lost. The docs label the feature experimental.
recommendation: For WP4, prefer an MDI tab with tiled or explicit viewer positions, or require the fixed tab to emulate the QMdiArea API. Add a WP3 check that a restored preset keeps its arrangement, or accept MDI placement explicitly.

'Grid' object has no attribute 'activeSubWindow'", "restored tabs ['GlueMdiArea', 'GlueMdiArea'] [0, 1]". title: Collapse list is incomplete, and stock moments are range-relative, NaN-propagating and display-only
verified: COLLAPSE_FUNCS is Mean, Median, Minimum, Maximum, Sum, Moment 1 and Moment 2. _on_collapse only sets an AggregateSlice on Image viewers of the same data and creates no dataset. mom1 and mom2 use the index within the selected sub-range, and np.maximum(nan, 0) propagates NaN, so one masked sample gives a NaN moment. This supports the WP2 layer_action design; the plan's list was just incomplete.
recommendation: Correct the list. Note in WP2 that stock moments are display-only, range-relative and NaN-sensitive; this supports the WP2 layer_action design.
evidence: Qt upstream/main profile_tools.py:31-37 (COLLAPSE_FUNCS) and 300-333 (_on_collapse builds AggregateSlice(slice(imin, imax), ...)). Core aggregate.py:8-26 (mom1 uses loc in range(n) over the passed subarray, with np.maximum). I ran mom1 on c[4:8] with the peak at 6 and c[5,1,1]=nan: [[2.0, 2.0], [2.0, nan]].

title: irispy gwcs_raster_clean branch breaks the glue-solar loader, and the plan does not track it
verified: The plan has no entry for irispy's gwcs_raster_clean work. On that branch, the unchanged glue-solar loader splits one raster file into 1496 2D datasets, loses wavelength from the world components and raises TypeError with stack=True. The branch is the user's own (all commits by Nabil Freij, last one 2026-09-08). It is pushed to LM-SAL/irispy but has no open PR, and irispy main instead merged FITS-TAB (#159). The risk is therefore real but depends on that branch landing; nothing breaks today. One small error in the recommendation: Tabular2D is used for time on this branch, and pointing comes from `_RasterSequenceCelestialTransform`.
recommendation: Add an irispy-compatibility gate to WP0/WP1: pin or CI-test against irispy main, and have `_raster_collection_data` accept both a sequence and a combined cube. Have `_GlueWCS` project out the extra time/step world axes, or wait for glue #2574. Note that irispy's per-scan Tabular2D pointing would supersede `stack_spectrogram_sequence` and the deferred 'per-scan absolute WCS' item (plan line 1014).

title: WP3 WCS serializer would not survive the raster move to gWCS
verified: On gwcs_raster_clean, `_create_tabular_wcs` is gone, so WP3's FITS -TAB record path would go unused for rasters. For a single file, WP3 falls back to the 'sliced'→'asdf' record and serializes fine. Only the combined multi-file raster gWCS fails ASDF, because the custom `_InverseRasterSequenceCelestialTransform` (_spectrograph_wcs.py:65) has no converter; line 46 holds the forward `_RasterSequenceCelestialTransform`. This only matters if that unmerged branch lands, and in that case the loader breaks first (finding 1).
recommendation: Record this as a WP3 risk. Either ask irispy (the user's branch) to ship ASDF converters for its custom models, or keep a fallback that re-reads from source files via the WP3 LoadLog path instead of embedding the WCS.

verified: Astropy builds objects as klass_gen(*component_values, *class_args, **kwargs, **class_kwargs), so the component values come first. This is latent, since every IRIS WCS kind has 0 class args. `pixel_to_world_values` calling list() on a 1D scalar result fails on both main and WP1.
recommendation: Index values[index] and route string indices through kwargs, or drop the n_args handling and document that the wrapper covers IRIS WCSs only.

title: Default rest wavelength is TWAVE, which shifts Mg II k velocities by +16 km/s; WP2 and WP6 disagree on this
verified: WP2 fills in and falls back to TWAVE (plan:732; wp2_moments_module.py:66-69; test_wp2_moments.py:37 expects '2796.20'). WP5 falls back to irispy metadata (plan:847), while WP6 rejects TWAVE (plan:879; wp6_fitting.py:134-135). TWAVE is the Mg II k window's nominal wavelength (2796.20 Å) against the vacuum line at 2796.35 Å, so velocities are biased by about +16 km/s. One detail is wrong: the Si IV 1394 bias is about -4 to -5 km/s, not +4 (TWAVE 1393.78 is longer than the 1393.755-1393.76 line); TWAVE matches the line list for Si IV 1403, C II 1336 and O I 1356.
recommendation: Use one policy in WP2, WP5 and WP6: an explicit override, otherwise the WP5 line-list entry that lies in the window (nearest TWAVE), otherwise no velocity. Never use TWAVE silently as a Doppler reference. Show the chosen line in the dialog.
evidence: Installed irispy 0.8.1 meta.py:193-198 returns TWAVE{n}. My header scan of 10 local L2 rasters showed TWAVE 2796.19995117 / 1393.7800293 / 1402.77001953 / 1335.70996094 in every file. mom.py on the 2018-01-02 raster printed 'TWAVE 2796.200, vacuum 2796.352; ... +16.30 km/s' and 'Si IV 1394 ... -5.38 km/s'. A single-Gaussian fit on that raster gave median centroid 2796.345 Å, which matches vacuum k. git show v0.8.1:examples/analysis/07_mg_ii_two_gaussian_fitting.py:129 has mg_ii_core = 279.6351 nm, and iris_lines.csv has 2796.35.

title: WP2 default 'blank wings = whole window' gives meaningless moments on real IRIS windows
verified: Plan:733 makes blank wings mean the whole window, and the prototype passes wings=None. On real full-size windows that holds several lines, the dialog defaults give meaningless moments. With ±0.5 Å wings around the vacuum rest, velocities come back near zero. irispy zeroes negative and non-finite samples (moments.py:135), which leaves a noise pedestal. For faint lines this inflates sigma even when wings are set.
recommendation: Require wings by default, for example ±0.5 Å or ±100 km/s around the chosen line-list rest wavelength. Move 'prefilled wings from a profile range' (plan line 1022) into v1. Document the clipping bias and suggest a min_intensity threshold.

With ±0.5 Å vacuum-rest wings it printed -0.5, +2.6 and +0.6 km/s. The windows (2790.65-2809.95, 1398.12-1406.67, 1331.77-1340.44 Å) contain k+h, O IV 1399.77/1401.16 and C II 1334.53/1335.71 (iris_lines.csv). synth.py (seeds 1 and 2) printed a clipped whole-window sigma of 0.243/0.245 and a ±0.3 Å sigma of 0.110/0.112, against a true 0.060.

title: WP6 ignores the source mask: missing spectra get finite fits and missing samples bias the fits, although parallel_fit_dask supports mask=
verified: WP6 clips at zero and applies nan_to_num (wp6_fitting.py:61). Missing samples (-200, flagged in the loader mask) therefore become zeros, and fully missing spectra get finite fits stuck at the seed centroid and width. Partly missing samples bias amplitude and sigma, while parallel_fit_dask's mask= (applied as zero weights) recovers the truth. I downgraded severity for three reasons: the plan already documents the limitation (plan:894-899, README:35), WP6 is not a milestone prerequisite, and plan:495 separately lists masks/quality as WP2/WP6 scope, which is an internal inconsistency.
recommendation: In v1, build mask = loader mask | ~isfinite, zero only those samples and pass mask= to parallel_fit_dask. Do not clip negative values. NaN out spectra that are fully masked. Add a noisy, zero-background synthetic test that would fail with clipping.
evidence: fit_real.py (2018 Si IV 1403, every 4th step, 43840 spectra) printed 'fully-missing with finite fit 1687/1687'; the fully-missing fits had amp ~3.7e-28, mu 1402.77 (the seed), sd 0.05. fit_test.py printed 24/24 (2014 Si IV) and 561/561 (sns Mg II), with 848 and 6919 partly missing spectra. synth.py printed 'miss->0 amp 3.655 sd 0.0069', 'clip0 bg 1.168 sd 0.0528' and 'mask= bg -0.102 amp 10.916 mu 1402.7981 sd 0.0609'. The mask handling is in .venv astropy/modeling/_fitting_parallel.py:505-510.

title: WP6 publishes invalid fits (negative sigma or amplitude) with no quality filtering
verified: The numbers reproduce: NaN fraction 0.000, sigma<0 6.0%, amp<0 11.2%. There is no quality filter, and the NaN fraction does not measure fit failure. However, negative sigma is mostly the Gaussian sign degeneracy rather than a failed fit: 62% of the sigma<0 fits have amp>0, median |sigma| 0.081 Å and centroids within ±0.5 Å of rest. Those fits should be published as |sigma|, not NaN'd wholesale. Gallery 01 sets negative sigma to NaN 'for the purpose of the color scale', not as a quality filter, and plan:892-893 already disclaims physical certification.
recommendation: Before publishing, NaN out fits with sigma <= 0, emission amplitude <= 0, a centroid outside the fit window or non-converged fit_info. Alternatively use a bounded fitter (TRFLSQFitter). Report the rejected fraction to the user.
evidence: fit_real.py printed 'NaN 0.000; sigma<0 0.060; amp<0 0.112' (43840 spectra) and, on a 10960-spectrum subset, 'sigma<0 fits: amp>0 frac 0.621, median |sigma| 0.081 A ..., centroid within +-0.5A of 1402.77 frac 0.985'. git show v0.8.1:examples/analysis/01_spectral_fitting.py:235-236 shows the colour-scale comment. Gaussian1D stddev bounds are (1.18e-38, None), yet LMLSQFitter results still came back negative.

title: CRISPEX Doppler image (wing difference) is missing from the plan and should come before WP6
verified: CRISPEX computes an in-program Doppler image: the difference between the image at the mirrored spectral position lp_dop = 2*lc - lp and the image at the current position. The plan has no Doppler image or Dopplergram product; its nearest item is the deferred 'red-blue asymmetry' moments follow-up (plan:1022), which the finding did not mention. CRISPEX has no moment or Gaussian fitting. Glue's elementwise arithmetic cannot take slices along the wavelength axis, so this is a genuine gap.
recommendation: Add a Doppler-image product (±Δv around the chosen line rest) to the first milestone, either as a WP5 blink companion or as a small layer_action. It is cheaper than WP6, robust for optically thick lines, and matches CRISPEX directly. Keep WP6 last.
evidence: git clone --depth 1 github.com/grviss/crispex (c0aa71e): crispex.pro:21000-21002 defines lp_dop, 21054-21059 computes dopslice, and 339 is the v1.6 changelog entry for 'in-program Doppler images'. grep -i -E 'gaussfit|mpfit|moment' crispex.pro found nothing. grep -i 'dopplergram|doppler image' IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md found nothing. The ITN 26 table of contents lists '7.2. Mg II Dopplergrams', and irispy v0.8.1 gallery 02:160 computes doppler = I(-50 km/s) - I(+50 km/s).

title: Plan never addresses optically thick lines (Mg II h/k, C II) for moments or Gaussian fits
verified: The plan never mentions optically thick lines, central reversals or proxy interpretation. The prototype labels its double Gaussian 'Mg II k2v/k2r' and offers moments and fits for any window. irispy gallery 07 itself calls the double Gaussian 'a simple fitted proxy ... rather than a full radiative-transfer inversion'. The fix is limited to documentation and labelling, so it does not block the quicklook goal.
recommendation: State in the briefs and user guide which products are physically interpretable (Si IV, O IV, Fe XII, Fe XXI, O I) and which are proxies (Mg II, C II). Do not label Mg II or C II centroids as 'velocity'. Narrow WP6 v1 to single Gaussians on thin lines. Defer the Mg II double Gaussian, or point users to red-blue asymmetry or k2/k3 feature products.
evidence: grep -n -i -E 'optically|thick|reversal|proxy' IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md returned nothing. wp6_fitting.py:132. git show v0.8.1:examples/analysis/07_mg_ii_two_gaussian_fitting.py:120-127. ITN 38 (https://iris.lmsal.com/itn38/analysis_lines_iris.html) says 'the optically thin lines are mostly observed to have a Gaussian shape'.

title: WP6 v1 leaves out the fit window and velocity map, the parts that make fit maps usable
verified: Plan:894 does exclude fit-window controls and velocity maps from WP6 v1. Fitting the whole Mg II window instead of the 2794-2798 Å crop raises the background by about 70 DN (40%) and lowers sigma by about 10%. The centroids, however, barely move (≤0.004 Å, about 0.4 km/s), so the claim that fit maps are unusable without a window is overstated for Mg II k. The multi-line-window impact on Si IV/C II was not measured.
recommendation: Reuse the WP2 rest/wings fields as the WP6 fit window and emit velocity (optical convention, same rest policy) in v1. Otherwise deprioritize WP6 until these land.

title: Saturated (Inf-flagged) samples are not caught by the WP2 saturation field, and one Inf breaks the whole WP6 fit
verified: The code behaviour is confirmed. irispy zeroes Inf (moments.py:135) before the saturation test (moments.py:176), so an Inf-flagged pixel is not NaN'd and shows reduced intensity. In WP6, one spectrum containing Inf poisons the shared mean-spectrum seed and NaNs almost every fit. The real-data impact is unverified: local L2 rasters are int16 (BSCALE 0.25, BZERO 7992, no BLANK), a format that cannot store Inf, and all show NSATPIX=0. How saturation is actually encoded on disk is therefore unknown.
recommendation: Detect Inf, or the TSATPXn header counts, before any clipping. Mask or NaN saturated spectra in both WP2 and WP6, and warn when TSATPXn > 0. Test with a synthetic Inf sample.
evidence: inf2.py printed 'saturation_limit=1e6: Inf pixel I 422.9 normal 659.9 Inf pixel NaN? False' and 'WP6 with 3 Inf samples in 1 of 18 spectra: finite centroid count 1 / 18'. The header probe printed '16 0.25 7992 None' plus NSATPIX/TSATPX1-7 = 0. ITN 26 section 6.4 (https://iris.lmsal.com/itn26/data_notes.html) says 'Saturated pixels are flagged as Inf'.

title: Intensities are in DN, not DN/s: variable exposures (AEC) are ignored in maps and thresholds
verified: The briefs publish DN, never mention exposure time, and the loader keeps per-exposure times in meta (irispy io/spectrograph.py:201-228). However, ITN 26 says varied AEC exposures occur 'only ... in extreme cases' such as flares. The local 2018 raster has constant 7.999 s exposures apart from one 0-s FUV step, and that step is already fully masked (-200), so masking covers it. Of the 7278 fully missing Si IV spectra, 548 come from that step. DN/s normalisation is a sensible option but not demonstrated to be necessary.
recommendation: Offer DN/s normalization using meta['exposure time'] (default on for the intensity/amplitude maps) and set 0-s steps to NaN. Document that thresholds are applied after normalization.
evidence: exp0.py printed 'Si IV 1403 exp-0 steps [157] fully masked there: [True] unique exp [0.0, 7.999]' and 'Mg II k 2796 ... unique exp [7.999]'. ITN 26 calibration page: 'This is the default for most active region observations, although different exposures are only used in extreme cases when very bright phenomena can lead to CCD saturation (e.g. a flare).'

title: WP2 moments maps cannot be saved, even with the WP3 prototype
verified: The WP2 moments dataset carries irispy's rebuilt 2-axis -TAB WCS (HPLT-TAB, HPLN-TAB). wp3_impl._tab_record indexes pixel_shape[2], so serialising a collection that contains moments maps raises IndexError and the whole save fails. WP3's brief tests only WP6 map round trips (plan:771-772). The WP2 brief says nothing about sessions.
recommendation: Either build the moments coords like WP6 (_GlueWCS(SlicedLowLevelWCS(raw_wcs, wavelength index 0))) instead of irispy's rebuilt WCS, or generalize _tab_record. Add a WP2 round-trip test next to the WP6 one.
evidence: sess.py printed 'moments coords _GlueWCS WCS ['HPLT-TAB', 'HPLN-TAB'] pixel_n_dim 2' and 'SERIALIZE FAILED IndexError tuple index out of range at wp3_impl.py 43 _tab_record'. IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp3_impl.py:41-43 loops 'for axis in (2, 3): ... wcs.pixel_shape[axis - 1]'.

title: No absolute wavelength-calibration caveat or offset for velocity products
verified: The plan offers velocity products (WP2) and Doppler display (WP5) relative to a rest wavelength, with no caveat about absolute wavelength calibration and no offset option. ITN 26 section 5.1 and ITN 38 section 4.2 both require a manual check against reference lines. I downgraded severity because the fix is a documentation caveat plus an optional offset and does not block quicklook use.
recommendation: Document the caveat in the product metadata and the guide. Allow an optional reference-line velocity offset (the WP5 override can carry it) instead of implying absolute velocities.
evidence: grep -n -i 'calibrat' IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md found no wavelength-calibration caveat. ITN 26 (https://iris.lmsal.com/itn26/calibration.html) section 5.1: 'accurate to only a few pixels, and should be manually checked ... Ni I 279.9474 nm ... O I 135.560 nm'. ITN 38 section 4.2: 'within an uncertainty of 5–10 km s-1'.

title: Full-size float64 residual attached to the source doubles memory and gets embedded in sessions
verified: fit_gaussians converts to float64, so the residual stored on the source is float64 at the source's full shape: 533 MB against a 266.5 MB float32 source for a 320x548x380 Mg II window. A component without _load_log is saved by value, so the residual would be embedded in a session. I confirmed the embedding by reading the code, not by saving a session.
recommendation: Make the residual opt-in and float32, or let users compare model and data on a selected pixel via the Profile Fit tab instead.
evidence: mgwin.py printed 'dtype float32 (320, 548, 380)'; 320*548*380*4 = 266.5 MB and *8 = 533.1 MB. stack4d.py printed 'residual ... float64'. .venv glue/core/state.py:1093-1101 (_save_component returns data=... unless _load_log). Plan:886.

title: Width convention (sigma) is never stated
verified: WP2 'width'/'velocity_width' and WP6 'width' are all 1-sigma standard deviations, and the plan never states the convention. ITN 38 works in FWHM = 2√(2 ln 2) σ. I did not verify the 1/e-width usage the finding cites.
recommendation: Name the components 'sigma' or 'sigma_velocity', or document the convention in the component metadata and the guide.
evidence: grep -n -i -E 'sigma|standard deviation|stddev|fwhm|1/e' IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md found nothing. irispy 0.8.1 moments.py:79 ('standard deviation') and 195-199. wp6_fitting.py:111 maps stddev_i to 'width'. ITN 38 quotes 'w_FWHM = 2 sqrt(2ln2) sigma'.

title: WP2 real-data test and 'compare with irispy' check nothing physical
verified: The irispy 0.8.1 bundled Mg II window (2793.44-2794.74 Å) contains no line core, and IN_WINDOW_REST 2794.09 is its midpoint, so '|median v| < 20' is a plumbing check. The WP6 synthetic cubes are noiseless. The prototypes README already concedes that physical validation is absent (README:30, 35). Under irispy 0.9.0 the bundled windows are full windows at a 10x-decimated 0.254 Å step, so the 'no line core' premise is specific to 0.8.1.
recommendation: Add a synthetic SpectrogramCube with a known Gaussian, including noise, missing samples and Inf, and assert centroid, sigma and velocity. Keep real rasters for shape and unit checks only.
evidence: test_wp2_moments.py:13 and 62. wp6_test_fitting.py:23-38 has no noise. fit_test.py printed 'Mg II k 2796 (187, 40, 52) wl 2793.44-2794.74'. win090.py printed for 0.9.0 'Mg II k 2796 ... wl 2793.42-2806.40 step 0.25460' and 'Si IV 1403 ... wl 1398.63-1405.75 step 0.25440'.

title: The '3D/4D shape contract' for WP6 is tested only for 3D in the recorded suite
verified: The recorded 17-test suite has no 4D stack case for WP6; the only 4D evidence is the historical probe log. When I ran the current prototype on a 4D stack it did work (maps (13,8,109), 3 links), so this is a coverage and wording gap, not a functional one.
recommendation: Move a 4D stack case into wp6_test_fitting.py, or reword the claim.
evidence: grep -n -i -E 'stack|4d|ndim' wp6_test_fitting.py review_20260905/test_plan_integration.py found nothing. wp6_chk_real_fixed.log:21-23. The recorded command printed '17 passed' (tests.log:16). stack4d.py printed 'stack (13, 8, 109, 17) maps (13, 8, 109) residual (13, 8, 109, 17) float64 links 3'.

title: Product meta keys do not match the WP5 rest-wavelength helper
verified: The WP5 helper reads meta['rest_wavelength'] or SGMeta.rest_wavelength. WP6 maps store 'rest_wavelength_angstrom', so the helper returns None and velocity conversion is unavailable. WP2 maps inherit SGMeta, so the helper returns TWAVE and ignores the rest wavelength the user entered.
recommendation: Write the rest actually used under the key WP5 reads, on both the WP2 and WP6 products.
evidence: metak.py printed 'WP2 maps meta SGMeta user rest 2794.09 -> WP5 helper 2796.1999511699996 Angstrom' and 'WP6 maps meta {... 'rest_wavelength_angstrom': 2794.09} -> WP5 helper None'. wp6_fitting.py:105. wp5_units.py:11-24.

title: irispy 0.9.0 was released before the plan update but was not validated
verified: irispy v0.9.0 (2026-09-10) is not recorded in the plan, and its moments/meta API change is compatible. The finding misses that the WP2/WP6 prototype tests break on 0.9.0. The bundled test files were renamed *_test.fits, and the prototypes match exact names; glue-solar main's conftest already handles the suffix. The files were also re-decimated to full windows, which invalidates plan:893 ('bundled windows omit line cores') and hard-coded numbers in the tests.
recommendation: Record 0.9.0 as the current release and re-run the WP2/WP6 checks against it before porting.
evidence: gh release list -R LM-SAL/irispy printed 'v0.9.0 Latest 2026-09-10T21:24:11Z'. git diff v0.8.1 v0.9.0 -- irispy/utils/moments.py irispy/meta.py. I ran the recorded command against a git-archive of v0.9.0: '3 failed, 11 passed, 3 errors' (StopIteration). After renaming the fixtures back: '2 failed, 15 passed', with 'assert 6545 == 5354' and 'assert 1405.754... < 1400'. glue_solar/conftest.py find_irispy_test_file ('Match both 0.8.1 filenames and irispy's later explicit _test suffix').

title: Default rest wavelength is the nominal window TWAVE, which biases Doppler velocities
verified: The plan (IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md:846-849) makes irispy metadata the default rest wavelength. irispy's SGMeta.rest_wavelength is just TWAVEn, in both 0.8.1 and 0.9.0. wp5_units.py:21 and :37 offer km/s whenever that value exists, and the WP2 dialog prefills it (wp2_moments_module.py:67). This gives a -16.3 km/s zero point for Mg II k and offers km/s for continuum windows (1343, 2832, 2826, 2814), which contradicts plan lines 450-451 and 879. The bias depends on the window: TWAVE equals the lab value for C II 1336, O I 1356 and Si IV 1403.
recommendation: Use this priority: explicit override, then the lab value from the packaged line list matched to TDESC, then unavailable. When a window holds several lines (C II 1334/1335, Mg II k/h), require the user to choose. Never offer km/s for continuum windows. Show the rest value in use. Apply the same rule to the WP2 prefill.
evidence: The installed irispy meta.py:194-198 returns float(TWAVE{_iwin}); `git show v0.9.0:irispy/meta.py` is still TWAVE-based. A header probe of the 2014 raster printed 'Mg II k 2796 2796.19995117', '2832 2832.70', '1343 1343.29', and '(2796.19995-2796.352)/2796.352*c = -16.30 km/s'. The archived plan measured the same effect (archive/2026-09-05/IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md:3433-3446, 'shift -16.07 km/s').

title: Sessions fail to restore when a Profile viewer uses a non-default x axis with a non-native display unit
verified: This is broader than reported. Any Profile viewer whose x_att is not the default axis fails GlueApplication.restore_session with ValueError, even with the native unit ('m' on a synthetic cube, 'Angstrom' on an IRIS raster). The cause is that x_att and x_display_unit share restore priority 1 (glue/viewers/profile/state.py:333-341), and update_from_dict only delays callbacks (core/state_objects.py:101-109). So every IRIS wavelength-spectrum panel, the core CRISPEX view, is unrestorable, and the 1D-only tests (test_line_positions.py:41-63, wp5_ll_session.py) cannot catch it.
recommendation: Add a WP0/core item: give x_att a higher restore priority than x_display_unit, or validate after the group is set. Make multi-axis IRIS Profile save/restore with km/s and nm an acceptance test in WP3 and WP5, and add a gated workaround if needed.
evidence: prof_restore2.py (synthetic WAVE/HPLT/HPLN cube, stock 1.27.0) printed 'm RESTORE FAILED ValueError value m is not in valid choices: ['deg', ...]'. The same failure appears with PYTHONPATH=core-profile:qt-profile. iris_restore3.py (IRIS Si IV 1403 raster + wp3 + wp5) printed 'RESTORE FAILED ValueError value Angstrom is not in valid choices: ['arcsec', 'arcmin', 'deg']', and the same for nm and km / s. _update_priority is identical on glue upstream main (gh api), origin/main, profile-slice and profile-wcsaxes.

title: WP3 cannot save WP2 moment maps (-TAB axes are hard-coded)
verified: WP2 moment maps carry a 2D HPLT-TAB/HPLN-TAB astropy WCS, from irispy make_spatial_template's cube.wcs.dropaxis. wp3_impl._tab_record hard-codes axes (2, 3), so saving any session that contains a moments map raises IndexError. The WP3 brief (plan:772) lists only WP6 map round trips. Severity is medium rather than high because WP2 is a 'later' extension and the fix is local.
recommendation: Take the -TAB axes and columns from the PSi_0/PSi_1/PSi_2 keys instead of assuming axes 2/3, or have WP2 rewrap as _GlueWCS(SlicedLowLevelWCS(raw, slices)) like WP6. Add a WP2 map round trip to the WP3 acceptance list.
evidence: moments_save.py (wp1 + wp3_impl + chk_wp2) printed 'moments inner WCS ['HPLT-TAB', 'HPLN-TAB'] (109, 8)'. The raster saved OK, but the moments save failed with 'wp3_impl.py, line 43, in _tab_record ... IndexError: tuple index out of range'. irispy/utils/_spectral.py:61-62 uses dropaxis.

title: A restored session loses SGMeta, so the rest wavelength and window properties disappear
verified: Glue's Data loader always builds a new Data and calls meta.update() with the filtered meta (glue/core/state.py _load_data_5), so even LoadLog-backed IRIS data come back with a plain OrderedDict. SGMeta properties (rest_wavelength, spectral_window) are lost, and km/s is no longer offered after reopening. Combined with wp3-wp5-2, a saved km/s Profile viewer could not restore anyway.
recommendation: At load time, have the loader write plain meta values (rest_wavelength in Angstrom, window name) and make WP5 read those, or add a scoped SGMeta saver. Add restored-session velocity to the WP3/WP5 acceptance tests.
evidence: meta_rt.py printed 'LoadLog True orig meta SGMeta 1402.77 Angstrom Si IV 1403', then 'restored meta OrderedDict None False n keys 398', then 'km/s offered orig: True restored: False'. The TWAVE1..n keys survive but _iwin does not.

title: The global Quantity saver makes any session with Quantity metadata require glue-solar
verified: wp3_impl.py:102-110 registers a process-wide Quantity saver/loader. A non-IRIS session with Quantity metadata saved under it will not open in plain glue (KeyError 'data'), and Quantity subclasses come back as plain Quantity. The plan already asks for 'scoped style/Quantity serialization' (plan:750), so this is a gap between the prototype and the plan, not a plan error. Stock 1.27.0 cannot save such metadata at all (TypeError), and #2597 is still open.
recommendation: Upstream a Quantity saver to glue-core (small PR next to #2597), or limit it to IRIS metadata. Record the portability trade-off in the WP3 brief.
evidence: q_save.py printed 'save-stock SAVE FAILED TypeError no implementation found for numpy.save', 'save-wp3 saved', "load-wp3 restored meta types {'exptime': 'Quantity', 'lat': 'Quantity'}" and "load-plain LOAD FAILED KeyError 'data'". gh pr view 2597 shows OPEN.

title: The WP5 unit converter replaces glue's default for all datasets and narrows their unit choices
verified: wp5_units.py:36-40 narrows the choices for every length or angle component of every dataset once it is installed as the global 'default' converter (line 51). The plan's text (846) does not require this narrowing, and it is not needed for the arcsec/Angstrom decision.
recommendation: Add km/s only for spectral components of datasets with a known rest wavelength, and otherwise fall through to super(). Drop the global narrowing, which also means less code.
evidence: A probe printed 'stock pc n 131 True True | rad has mas True', then after importing wp5_units: "wp5 pc ['Angstrom', 'nm'] | wp5 rad ['arcsec', 'arcmin', 'deg']".

title: WP3 acceptance leaves out viewers, subsets, links and WP4 coordination
verified: The WP3 checklist (plan:757-775) is Data-level only, and wp3chk_test_sessions.py serializes bare DataCollections. WP4 sync is installed per app by wrapping new_data_viewer (wp4_common.py:92-148), with nothing re-attaching it after restore. The plan does acknowledge the need elsewhere: line 494 says 'validate full IRIS application sessions', line 749 admits the tests 'do not ... prove a full coordinated quicklook session', and WP4's test item (plan:861) includes 'serializable links'. What is missing is an explicit application-level acceptance item plus a coordination re-attach step.
recommendation: Add application-level acceptance: image/profile/whisker viewer states, point/ROI subsets, WCS + link_hpc + WP4 identity links, and coordination re-attached after restore. Make each of WP2/WP4/WP5/WP6 include its own save/reopen test.
evidence: Plan lines 494, 749, 767-775 and 861, read directly. wp3chk_test_sessions.py:32-35 has _round_trip on a DataCollection. wp4_common.py:92-148 has sync_slices/_install_slice_sync, which only wraps app.new_data_viewer. The reviewer's link_session.py result on core-ape14 was not re-run.

title: WP4's full-shape nearest-index components bloat file-referencing sessions
verified: Nearest-index components added by link_time have no LoadLog, so file-referencing sessions embed the full broadcast int32 arrays at about 5.3 bytes per pixel after base64. That is 18x on the tiny fixture pair and scales to GB for real SJI/raster sizes. This would stop the milestone's 'reopened session' on a representative dataset unless the indices are stored compactly. Severity is raised to high on that basis; the fix itself is local.
recommendation: Store compact 1D index arrays (for example a Component subclass with its own __gluestate__ that re-broadcasts on load, or recompute from Time on restore). Add a real-size session budget to the WP3/WP4 tests.
evidence: size_probe.py (SJI 1330 (52,40,37) + sns C II 1336 raster (187,40,18), wp3 factories) printed 'file-referencing session bytes before/after link_time: 66525 1197291'. The added 1,130,766 B over 211,600 px is about 5.34 B/px, consistent with int32 plus base64. The reviewer's 67,440 to 1,715,976 came from a different window. The embedded-mode Time/mask sizes were not re-checked.

title: The 11-line list omits standard IRIS lines and wavelength-calibration references
verified: iris_lines.csv has 11 lines and omits Fe XII 1349.40, whose window is in the test raster (TDESC3 'Fe XII 1349'). It also omits the Mg II triplet (vacuum 2798.75/2798.82), S IV 1404.81/1406.02 and O IV 1404.78. Young, Tian & Jaeggli (2015) give Fe XXI 1354.106±0.023 Å against the list's 1354.08, although ITN 38 itself labels it 1354.08. The labels are inconsistent ('C II 1335' where the TDESC is 'C II 1336'). This is a label list, so omissions do not corrupt numbers, hence low.
recommendation: Add Fe XII 1349.40, the Mg II triplet, O IV 1404.78, S IV 1406.02, Ni I 2799.474 and S I 1401.515. Use 3-decimal NIST/CHIANTI values with a source column and consistent names matching TDESC.
evidence: The NIST ASD query returned Mg II air 2797.930/2797.998 (vacuum about 2798.75/2798.82), S IV 1404.808/1406.009, and Fe XII 1349.40 (obs). The ApJ 799 218 abstract (WebFetch) gives '1354.106 ± 0.023 Å'. twave.py printed 'Fe XII 1349 1349.43'.

title: The velocity display ignores the Level-2 wavelength-calibration caveat
verified: ITN 38 §4.2 says the Level-2 wavelength calibration should always be checked manually against strong neutral lines, stable to within 5-10 km/s. It names O I (printed as '1335.60', evidently 1355.60), S I 1401.515 and Ni I 2799.474. The plan's WP5 has no disclosure and no per-dataset offset. For a quicklook this is mainly a docs/UI caveat, hence low.
recommendation: State in the UI and docs that velocities are relative to the uncorrected Level-2 scale. Optionally add a per-dataset wavelength offset, stored as plain metadata, next to the rest override.
evidence: curl of iris.lmsal.com/itn38/analysis_lines_iris.html, text line 108 (quoted). grep of the plan for 'calibrat|2799|Ni I|S I 1401' finds only lines 495 and 898, which are unrelated to the WP5 velocity scale.

title: CRISPEX's live Doppler (red-minus-blue wing) image is not in the plan
verified: CRISPEX computes a live Doppler image: the image at the mirror position lp_dop = 2*lc - lp minus the current image, shown in its own window with its own scaling. The plan, the prototypes and the archive never mention it; they have only offline moments and a deferred red-blue asymmetry item (plan:1022). The plan should either add it or explicitly defer it.
recommendation: Decide explicitly: add it to WP5 (for example a derived Δλ-indexed wing-difference cube built from the chosen rest wavelength, viewed with ordinary sliders) or list it as deferred or a non-goal.
evidence: crispex.pro:20999-21001 (lp_dop = 2*lc - lp), :21054-21060 (dopslice difference), :3331 ('Doppler image' window) and :339 ('in-program Doppler images'). grep -i 'doppler image|dopplergram|wing difference' over the plan and IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/archive, review_20260923 and README gives no hits.

title: The UI entry points for the rest override and the line list were dropped
verified: The current WP5 brief requires an 'explicit Angstrom override' and a packaged line list, but it names no UI entry point and does not reference the existing wp5_override.py prototype. The archived plan had a 'Set rest wavelength…' layer_action, a 'Plugins -> IRIS: add line list' menubar action, and docs quantifying the 16 km/s Mg II k offset.
recommendation: Restore both actions, and the prototype reference, to the WP5 checklist.
evidence: grep of the plan for 'Set rest|add line list|wp5_override' finds nothing. The WP5 references are at plan:833-837. The archive has these at archive/2026-09-05/IRIS_GLUE_GAP_PLAN.md:3413, 3622, 3739, 3741 and 3761. IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp5_override.py:13 contains the layer_action.

title: CRISPEX blink/playback modes and scaling are only partly mapped
verified: CRISPEX has LOOP/CYCLE (ping-pong)/BLINK temporal playback modes, spectral blink between lp_blink and lp_blink_init, main/reference blink, and image scaling modes 'based on first/current/per time step'. glue-qt playback only goes forward or back, with wrap. The plan maps spectral and layer blink but not CYCLE or temporal BLINK, and it does not make the scaling policy an option.
recommendation: List the temporal-blink and cycle modes as deferred or accepted gaps, and make the scaling policy (shared vs per-position) an explicit option of the two-wavelength blink.
evidence: crispex.pro:13601-13624 (CYCLE/BLINK), :13571-13574 (spectral blink toggle), :13859-13880, :4221-4230 and :7950-7955 (imagescale modes). ~/Git/glue-qt glue_qt/viewers/common/data_slice_widget.py:81-89 and :146-155 (back/stop/forw).

title: WP3 sliced-WCS record crashes on NumPy integer slice indices
verified: wp3_impl.py:65 uses isinstance(s, int), so a SlicedLowLevelWCS built with a numpy integer index fails to serialize.
recommendation: Use isinstance(s, numbers.Integral) and int(s), and also cast slice start, stop and step to int.
evidence: A probe printed 'int OK [0, [None, None, None], [None, None, None]]' and then "int64 FAILED AttributeError 'numpy.int64' object has no attribute 'start'".

title: The line-list style-editor patch hides editors for other Profile artists
verified: glue-qt's on_artist_add looks up the artist class exactly in a dict and hits 'else: return' on a miss. That drops the style editor for unknown or subclassed Profile artists, and also for any later artists in the same batch. wp5_linelist_mod.py:116-118 turns ProfileViewer's single editor class into such a dict.
recommendation: Use a dict subclass with a ProfileLayerStyleEditor fallback, or scope the change to IRIS artists.
evidence: ~/Git/glue-qt glue_qt/core/layer_artist_model.py:364-369 (the same on origin/main). ProfileViewer._layer_style_widget_cls = ProfileLayerStyleEditor at glue_qt/viewers/profile/data_viewer.py:19.

title: The blink tool puts a permanent spinbox in every Image viewer toolbar
verified: 'image:blink' is appended to ImageViewer.tools globally (wp5_blink.py:67-68), and the tool's __init__ adds the interval QSpinBox to viewer.toolbar (line 38). So every Image viewer shows the spinbox. The blinked layer set is frozen at activation (line 48 comment).
recommendation: Show the interval control only while blink is active, or keep one fixed or settable interval.
evidence: wp5_blink.py:31-38, :48 and :67-68, read directly. This was not run in a GUI.

title: The WCSAxes line position uses a brentq root find where interpolation would do
verified: _world_to_profile_pixels already samples a finite, strictly monotonic trace (wp5_linelist_mod.py:90-95), so np.interp on the sorted trace would replace the per-line brentq, which calls the full WCS at each iteration. The result is exact for a linear spectral axis. IRIS wavelength axes are linear WAVE; -TAB is used only for pointing.
recommendation: Replace it with np.interp(value, trace_sorted, pixels_sorted).
evidence: wp5_linelist_mod.py:85-100. The raster WCS ctype is ['WAVE', 'HPLT-TAB', 'HPLN-TAB'] (moments_save.py output).

title: The -TAB rebuild depends on irispy internals that a WIP gWCS branch replaces
verified: irispy #159 (FITS-TAB pointing) merged at 2026-08-05T02:20Z. origin/gwcs_raster_clean is 12 commits ahead, last commit 2026-09-08, uses _create_raster_gwcs/_combine_raster_cubes, and has no PR. title: Slit overlay from raw SLTPX1IX never appears on the matched fixture; pixel_stride fixes the wrong problem
verified: The headline is wrong: the fixtures are stride-10 decimations, not crops, so pixel_stride=10 does put the slit on the image. SLTPX1IX 187 becomes 18.7, next to CRPIX1 18.45 on the 37-px SJI; 2023 values 549/1269 become 54.9/126.9 on the 178-px SJI. The WCS projection to x≈21-23 is an artifact: the fixture keeps native CDELT after decimation. What remains valid: the SLTPX1IX 0- vs 1-based convention is unresolved (CRISPEX uses it as CRPIX, ITN41 plots it unshifted), and irispy tags these pixel values as arcsec.
recommendation: Derive the overlay as CRISPEX does: raster slit world coordinates at the matched exposure, projected through the SJI WCS of the matched frame. Use SLTPX1IX only as a cross-check after the base convention is confirmed on full-size real data. Drop pixel_stride from the production API and handle fixture decimation in tests.

verified: The plan does assign these to WP4: the feature table (plan:491) says 'choose the driving dataset, compute nearest exposure plus signed offset, define gap/no-match/tie rules', and sequence step 4 (plan:591-595) repeats it. title: Wrapping app.new_data_viewer misses session-restored viewers; the repo already has a per-viewer hook pattern
verified: No viewer-creation hub message exists in core or Qt (local, origin or upstream main). Session restore builds viewers with cls(session, state=...) and calls add_widget directly, so a wrapped app.new_data_viewer never sees restored viewers; a restored app also lacks the private wrapper. Registered viewer tools are instantiated in initialize_toolbar via the ToolbarInitializer metaclass for every construction, including restore. That is the pattern FrameTimeTool already uses on main. The plan (820-823) acknowledges the wrapping but not the session-restore gap.
recommendation: Implement sync participation as a registered Image/Profile viewer tool (the solar:frame_time pattern) that registers with one controller per data collection and unregisters in close(). Remove the method wrapping and the private app attribute.

title: link_time fails for V34 (flipped) rasters because step times descend
verified: For V34 observations (STEPS_AV < -0.01), irispy reverses times and data along the step axis. No V34 fixture exists, so this was reproduced with synthetic descending times.
recommendation: Argsort the reference, match against the sorted times, and map the result back to the original indices. Test with descending step times.

title: WP7 AIA crop fails for any IRIS field of view with an off-limb corner
verified: The finding holds, and the failure is broader than stated. Off-limb corners become NaN whenever the AIA frame's observer or obstime differs from the IRIS Earth frame at STARTOBS, which is always true for real AIA data. With an Earth observer and only a +5 s obstime change, the corners at 1000 arcsec are already NaN and submap raises ValueError. The brief (plan 928-931) prescribes only propagate_with_solar_surface. The synthetic test uses the same observer and obstime (test_context.py:41-46), so it hides the bug. The error is caught as a message box (context_chk.py:166-171), but limb and prominence pointings cannot get AIA context.
recommendation: In the brief, require `with propagate_with_solar_surface(), SphericalScreen(iris_observer, only_off_disk=True):` around the transform. Add a test that uses an off-limb FOV and an AIA frame whose observer is not Earth.

'earth +5s' gives [700.01 900 nan nan] and submap ValueError '...contain NaN values...'. 'sdo +5s' gives propagate [700.17 900.21 nan nan], and adding SphericalScreen(only_off_disk=True) gives [700.17 900.21 1000.24 1000.24]. See context_chk.py:106-110 and test_context.py:41-46.

title: WP8: clicking Load during a rescan loads from the replaced observation list
verified: Reproduced. `ok` stays enabled while a rescan runs, because set_directory never disables it (wp8_proto.py:31-46). finalize() calls processEvents per pick (iris.py:300-303), which delivers the queued _scanned. That call replaces self.observations and repopulates while the picks still hold the old indices. Stopping the worker at the start of finalize would not fix this, because _stop_scan does not bump _scan_id and so the partial result is still delivered. Disabling Load while scanning is the robust fix.
recommendation: Add to the brief: disable `ok` while scanning, or have finalize() first stop the scan and bump _scan_id. Add a test that clicks Load while a slow rescan is running.
evidence: Scratch test test_v_wp8.py::test_f2_load_during_rescan. Before the rescan, the pick was (3,'raster','C II 1336') for obsid 3400109360 with 2 raster files. The rescan was gated with threading.Event, then worker.wait() and ok.click(). Output: 'calls [([], ['C II 1336'])] populate [True, True]', 1 passed. git status clean.

title: WP8 Stop, Cancel, close and rescan freeze the GUI for the whole directory walk
verified: The freeze reproduces: scan_directory sorts the whole rglob/is_file walk before it first polls stop (wp8_scan.py:136-141), and _stop_scan calls worker.wait() on the GUI thread (wp8_proto.py:51). However, the plan is not unaware of this. Lines 498 and 968-969 explicitly record that the walk is not interruptible. The inaccuracy is only that 'delay stop' understates the effect, which is a GUI-wide freeze. It matters only for large or network trees; polling stop inside the walk is the cheap fix.
recommendation: Poll stop() inside the enumeration, e.g. collect paths in a loop that breaks on stop(), then sort. Say in the brief that wait() runs on the GUI thread, so a stop that is not cooperative freezes the application rather than just delaying.
evidence: Scratch test_f3_reject_blocks_during_walk, with Path.is_file slowed to 0.1 s on the iris_tree fixture: 'reject blocked 1.16s, is_file calls 11', 1 passed. Plan 498: 'document that directory enumeration/current header reads can delay stop'. Plan 968-969: 'initial sorted directory walk is not interruptible in this prototype'.

title: WP7 GOES satellite rule is unspecified, and GOES-19 is unreachable with released sunpy
verified: Several details are confirmed. Plan 920-921 does not state a satellite rule, and the prototype takes the first satellite (context_chk.py:43-44). GOES-19 is unreachable with released sunpy, and live SatelliteNumber values are int64 while the mock uses strings (test_context.py:65). However, NOAA's current X-ray primary is GOES-18, with GOES-19 as secondary, so post-2025 searches still return the primary XRS satellite and the missing GOES-19 is not a functional gap today. The finding's claims about GOES-19 becoming operational GOES-East in April 2025 and GOES-16 being turned off are not supported by the cited SWPC page.
recommendation: State the rule in the brief (for example, prefer the NOAA primary or let the user choose with a.goes.SatelliteNumber). Note that GOES-19 needs sunpy>=8.1. Mock with int64 satellite numbers.

title: Other global-patch prototypes to port only as scoped code (WP3, WP1)
verified: Importing wp3_impl does register a process-global `@saver(u.Quantity)`/`@loader` and patches `_GlueWCS.__gluestate__`/`__setgluestate__` and `L/M.VisualAttributes`. `L.image_data`/`L.raster_data` are rebound only by the explicit `install_browser_factories()`, not on import. title: Link 'order' does not decide the WCSLink versus time-link tie; memory-address set order does
verified: The technical claim is confirmed. discover_links relaxes to the minimum hop count; at equal cost the first accepted link wins (cost >= depth skips later ones). Links are iterated from a set of object-hashed links, so the winner is not controlled by add order. The kind is wrong, though: the plan never claims order control; only the scratch probe labelled results by order. The proposed rule is too broad: equal-hop alternatives are harmless when they compute the same value, and the rule should forbid equal-hop links that give different values for one target.
recommendation: Record in the plan that glue gives no ordering guarantee. A correct graph must never have two links of equal hop count that reach the same component ID from one dataset. The regression test should run every permutation plus a loop that perturbs memory allocation.

My runs of test_tie: winners with fixed add order and perturbed allocation ['ComponentLink','ComponentLink','identity','identity','identity','identity'] (0.8.1) and ['identity','ComponentLink','ComponentLink','ComponentLink','identity','ComponentLink'] (0.9.0). title: Loader stores masks as int64 (2x the data) and the stack keeps a redundant in-RAM mask
verified: Every IRIS mask component, stacked or not, is stored as int64 (8 B per element, twice the float32 data): Component() calls coerce_numeric, which does bool.astype(int). The stack also rebuilds mask = ~isfinite(output). The plan does not treat the stack mask as undocumented: WP9 (line 996) already says 'NaN/mask reconstruction', and solar main tests assert that the stack mask component exists (test_importer.py:171-180). Storing it as uint8 keeps that contract, while dropping it breaks a tested behavior. The 19.6 GB figure for all windows is a linear extrapolation that was not run.
recommendation: WP1: drop the stack mask component, because NaN already encodes it; if a mask is needed, use a derived component. Store unstacked masks as uint8/int8, which coerce_numeric leaves unchanged. Thresholds: retained RSS at most 6 B/element and peak at most 10 B/element after raster_data; all 7 windows of the 99-scan raster stacked under 12 GB peak on a 24 GB machine. If this holds, Dask can stay deferred for these datasets.
evidence: glue/core/component.py:53 calls coerce_numeric. glue/utils/array.py:158-160 converts bool to int (also at origin/main dae530c3). I observed Component(bool).dtype = int64 and Component(uint8).dtype = uint8. The loader adds the mask at iris.py:79-80@plan and the stack builds it at stack_spectrograms.py:79. s1_mg_stack.txt shows maxrss 9,696,706,560 B with memmapped=1.86 GB and masks=3.71 GB; s1_all_stack_25/50 show 5.22/10.07 GB. title: WP4 nearest-index components make 'file-referencing' sessions 5,400x larger
verified: link_time adds Nearest components as broadcast views, which have no LoadLog entry, so glue's Component saver writes them out in full. With WP4 links, the file-referencing session grows from 235 KB to 1.28 GB on real data. On the fixtures it grows from 67 KB to 1.7 MB, which already exceeds WP3's 'under 100 KB' target, so fixture tests could catch this. The 3.6 GB and 8.6 GB session sizes (and the 9-window figure) are extrapolations; the 9-window number does not appear in any log.
recommendation: WP4: persist only the 1-D per-exposure/per-frame index vectors, for example as a small index dataset joined by pixel links, or recompute them from Time on restore through a custom saver. WP3 threshold: the quicklook session (SJI plus 2 windows plus WP4 links) is at most 1 MB and saves in at most 2 s.
evidence: wp4_common.py:68,71 add the components with np.broadcast_to. glue/core/state.py:1096-1101 saves context.do(component.data) when there is no _load_log. s4_session_si.txt shows 'SESSION with WP4 components: 1277702953 bytes in 5.1s', 'without ... 235111 bytes' and peak footprint 13149137216. I reran find-wp3-wp5/size_probe.py and got '67440 1715976'. Record sizes are consistent with int32 arrays of shape (1600,417,262) and (400,417,388) after np.save plus base64.

title: The WP6 float64 residual cube doubles RAM and embeds hundreds of MB in sessions
verified: WP6 casts the cube to float64 and stores cube minus model as a float64 residual component on the source, twice the float32 window. Because that component is not LoadLog-backed, it is embedded in sessions. Almost all of the 640 MB fit session is the residual: the maps account for about 9 MB, and the 'fit products removed' comparison also removed the maps. The 2.96 GB figure for sit-and-stare Mg II k is arithmetic (370,296,000 × 8 B), not a measurement.
recommendation: WP6: store the residual as float32 in the source's dtype, or make it opt-in or recomputable from the parameter maps. WP3 threshold: fit products add at most 2x the 2-D map bytes to a session unless the user opts into embedding the residual.
evidence: wp6_fitting.py:61 has np.asarray(cube, dtype=float), :89 returns cube - model, and :123 calls add_component(Component(residual)). s3_fit_session_si.txt shows residual ('float64', 472770560) = 320*548*337*8, 'SESSION with fit products: 639802769 bytes' and 'removed: 53703 bytes'.

title: The stock 'Add large data set?' modal (default Cancel) blocks quicklook's Profile viewer
verified: The modal is real, and accepting its default is worse than just an empty viewer: after Cancel, glue closes the viewer and new_data_viewer returns None, so quicklook() raises AttributeError at wp4_common.py:196 (profile.state). This affects the sit-and-stare windows and the 99-scan stack, which are above 1e8 elements. The 2018 rasters (5.9e7) are below the threshold. The user can press OK or tick 'Don't show again', and plan line 1109 only says to mock modals in headless tests.
recommendation: WP4: add IRIS data to the quicklook Profile viewer without the modal, for example by setting large_data_size=None on that viewer, and keep a size notice non-blocking. Run the real-size quicklook test without the monkeypatch.
evidence: glue viewer.py:200-203 warns with default='Cancel'. glue-qt profile/data_viewer.py:25 sets large_data_size = 1e8, and data_viewer.py:6,123 routes warn to dialogs.warn, which calls exec_() (dialogs.py:20-37). application_base.py:87-92 closes the viewer and returns None when add_data returns False. My probe verify-followup-2/test_modal_cancel.py (WP1 root, warn returning False) printed 'RESULT raised AttributeError 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'state''. Sizes: 370,296,000, 174,806,400 and 463,999,536 elements.

title: Slider latency grows linearly with exposure index (the -TAB WCS), reaching 0.36 s per synced step
verified: The latency is already there on solar main without WP4: each slice change resets WCSAxes (ImageViewer._on_slice_change -> _set_wcs), and the per-point cost of the irispy -TAB pixel_to_world grows linearly with the exposure index. This is a property of the irispy/wcslib -TAB table, so the fix belongs in WP1/the loader, not WP4. WP4 sync then adds roughly 0.1 s on top of that. The linearize-or-cache remedy has not been tested.
recommendation: WP1: make slicing along the exposure axis cheap, for example by caching or linearizing the spatial -TAB table per exposure for WCSAxes. WP4 threshold: one SJI or exposure slider step with 3 synced image viewers redrawn in at most 0.25 s at any index (at least 4 fps playback) on the 1600-exposure sit-and-stare.
evidence: My rerun of test_raster_slider on the solar-main root gave 'SLIDER ... 1:0.032+0.039 ... 800:0.097+0.048 ... 1599:0.162+0.065 5:0.033+0.030'. My tabcost.py gave 0.03/0.24/0.44/0.84 ms per 1000 points at steps 1/400/800/1599 (irispy WCS ['WAVE','HPLT-TAB','HPLN-TAB']). glue/viewers/image/viewer.py:96-98. s2_quicklook.txt shows SJI frame 1 at 0.102+0.078 s and frame 399 at 0.251+0.108 s. s2_syncprofile.txt shows SYNC 0.168-0.290 and LOOKUP 0.000s.

title: WP2 moments block the GUI thread for seconds on sit-and-stare windows
verified: MomentsDialog.run calls line_moments synchronously on the GUI thread, and WP2 has no responsiveness requirement. The measured blocking is 0.6 s on the 2018 windows and 2.2 s on sit-and-stare Si IV; about 4.7 s for Mg II k is an extrapolation. This is a single freeze during an explicit analysis action, not during browsing, so it is low severity for a quicklook. Moving it to the existing Worker, as WP6 does, is reasonable polish.
recommendation: WP2: run moments above about 5e7 elements in the existing Worker, as WP6 does, and add the maps on the main thread. Threshold: at most 0.5 s of GUI-thread blocking and a peak increase of at most 3x the float32 window bytes.
evidence: chk_wp2/wp2_moments_module.py:87 calls self.moments = line_moments(...) inside run() with no Worker or thread. Plan lines 721-743 give no timing requirement. s3_moments_SiIV1403.txt shows '0.6s on the calling (GUI) thread' with maxrss 2878029824, and s3_moments_sns_si.txt shows '2.2s ... rss_delta_after=2.74 GB maxrss=5.56 GB'.

verified: Confirmed: the criterion only asks to 'Record' sizes, latency and memory. No WP checklist owns it and no numbers are set; the only other mention is the Dask row, which says 'First-milestone performance evidence'. Proposed thresholds on the 24 GB reference machine, warm cache, offscreen:

title: Intermittent hard crash while stepping time with Profile + Image viewers of one IRIS raster (no owner)
verified: With threaded profiles, test_12 (sit-and-stare Si IV, 2 Image viewers + 1 Profile viewer, slice set 100→300) crashes the process intermittently. It crashed in 4 of 8 fresh threaded runs (1 SIGBUS, 3 SIGTRAP) and in 0 of 4 runs with ComputeWorker.start disabled. The plan has no thread-safety item (plan:452-456; grep for thread/crash/race finds only WP6/WP8 worker text). A WCS race is plausible but not proven: in my SIGBUS the main thread was in wcsp2s while the workers were in numpy, not in wcs.py, so the _GlueWCS lock is an untested mitigation.
recommendation: Add a WP4/WP1 robustness task: serialize _GlueWCS pixel/world calls with a lock in glue-solar (D2), or give worker threads their own WCS copy. Add a threaded playback stress test (profile + image viewers, many slice steps) to the first-milestone gate and report the race upstream. A lighter stress test (scan-0 raster, 60 steps) did not reproduce the crash in 3 runs, so gate on the sit-and-stare scenario.

title: Five CRISPEX journey steps have no owner in the plan
verified: Three steps truly lack an owner: per-scan -200 fill handling, the cross-window (Si IV vs Mg II) blink, and the all-slit-positions SJI overlay. Scaling is owned generically: first-milestone criterion plan:447 ('own wavelength grids and scaling') and the WP4 preset (plan:485, 'useful axes/scaling'). The specific histogram-opt/gamma controls are not. Movie export is tracked as unscheduled (plan:396, 1017, 1051), and later slit work includes physical distance coordinates and session support (plan:497, 619). Exposure time is a first-milestone criterion (plan:427) and the blink interval is in WP5 (plan:493). Only the playback frame range, the timing offset, derived-data export and slope/ruler tools are absent.
recommendation: Add rows to the keyboard-level table with owners: scaling and fill to WP1/WP5, cross-window blink to WP5, all-positions overlay to WP4, export to WP2/WP6 plus later slit work, exposure/playback controls to WP4. Alternatively, list any of them explicitly under deferred work.
evidence: Plan lines as cited. IRIS-9 step 2 (crispex-replay/iris9.txt:104) asks only for histogram opt/gamma and says nothing about -200 fill; Boulder Ex#3 (boulder.txt:135) is SJI scaling. A grep of the plan for 'gamma|percentile|histogram|shortcut|EXPTIME|stretch|scaling' hits only :248, 447, 485, 493 and 858.

title: Per-scan rasters keep -200 DN fill as data, which breaks default scaling and Mean profiles
verified: Per-scan rasters publish the raw flux, with -200 fill kept as data and the mask only as a separate component. The stack converts masked samples to NaN, so auto-limits and Mean profiles differ between the two load paths. The plan mentions masked samples only in the end-to-end demo (plan:453) and WP2 tests (plan:740). No WP owns display or statistics masking for per-scan data, and #53's transparent-NaN rendering cannot help because per-scan data contains no NaN.
recommendation: WP1: publish masked per-scan samples as NaN, as the stack already does, or exclude the mask from limits and statistics. Test auto-limits, Mean profiles and moment inputs on a real per-scan raster. This is a precondition for IRIS-9 3.3.1 step 2.
evidence: My independent run on scan 0 Si IV of 4000005156 printed 'n-200 3050445 frac 0.1153 nan 0', 'min at (32,400,:) -200.0 n-200 there 28', 'mask==(f==-200) True' and 'limits 99.5 -200.0 12.75' (the finding reported 11.5, which is within sampling variation). glue_solar/sources/loaders/iris.py:78-80; stack_spectrograms.py:53-56 (NaN). The irispy 0.8.1 mask is computed only when memmap=False (io/spectrograph.py:250-251); BAD_PIXEL_VALUE_SCALED=-200 (utils/constants.py:18).

title: F095 cursor lock is a must, but plan:432-433 calls lock optional; no tier makes the lock follow time
verified: There is no contradiction. plan:432-433 requires 'Keep a fixed selection during time stepping' and makes only hover-only follow/lock optional. The plan already records that the selected point does not drive other viewers' fixed indices or draft slice profiles, and assigns this to WP4 (plan:486, 783-784, 811-812). What holds is that every tier lacks this, and that WP4's prototype hooks only ImageViewerState slices. A further gap is unspecified: a Pixel pick in a sit-and-stare exposure×slit image also fixes exposure, so the lock semantics need definition.
recommendation: Keep F095 at [must], with status 'hold exists; time-coupled lock missing (WP4)'. Reword plan:432-433 so that only hover-follow (F094) is optional. Specify that a sit-and-stare lock fixes slit only and that WP4 must drive the λ–t slit slider and the Slice-profile scan/exposure slider.

title: The WP5 blink scope misses the IRIS-9 cross-window blink (Si IV 1403 vs Mg II k 2796)
verified: The plan and WP5 define blink as two wavelength indices 'in one cube' (plan:447-450, 856-859). CRISPEX's IRIS-9 and Boulder blinks work because a Level-3 file concatenates windows into one spectral axis, and Level-3 is a permanent non-goal. glue-solar loads each window as a separate Data, and even with step/slit identity links the Mg II layer is disabled in a Si IV-referenced viewer. So neither the planned same-cube blink nor the WP5 layer blink meets IRIS-9 3.3.1 step 3 or Boulder Ex#7.
recommendation: WP5: define the blink as alternating (dataset, wavelength index) pairs on a shared spatial grid, for example by switching the viewer's reference data and slice, and keep the same-cube case. Test it on 4000005156 Si IV 1403 / Mg II k 2796 at about 2 fps.

Plan:621-622 and 1011 list Level-3 as a non-goal.

title: No SJI overlay of all raster slit positions; WP4 draws only the current frame's slit
verified: WP4 ports only a per-frame current-slit subset. Neither the plan, the prototypes nor stock glue offers a static overlay of all raster slit positions, which CRISPEX draws by default. SJI aux slit x cannot supply the positions (16 distinct over 32 frames against 64 steps). For dense rasters such an overlay mostly shows the field of view, and the moving current slit already gives the timing cue, so this is a parity gap for sparse rasters (IRIS-9's 4-step flare), not a blocker.
recommendation: WP4: add a toggleable static 'raster positions' overlay computed from the raster's step world coordinates and mapped into SJI pixels through WP1 link_hpc/WCS. Keep the per-frame current-slit subset as the timing indicator.
evidence: IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp4_common.py:16-33; plan:426 and 788-794. crispex-replay/results_iii.jsonl step 07a (mask_columns [650], slit_x 649.89, distinct 16, n_frames 32) and 07b (no API). iris9.txt:117-118 ('4 raster positions superimposed'); boulder.txt:127-130.

title: Derived products cannot be exported usefully (moment maps lose WCS/Time; x–t diagrams are not Data)
verified: Confirmed: the glue FITS exporter writes a WCS header only for astropy WCS and skips non-numerical components, so a _GlueWCS moment map exports without WCS or Time. HDF5, FITS Table and VOTable fail on datetime64, and CSV and IPAC reject >1D data. WP2/WP6 have no export item. However, derived maps persist inside glue through WP3 sessions, and the plan already records that the PV tool is a legacy standalone widget and points to PathSlicedData for later slit work (plan:497, 617-619). Moments are declared non-prerequisite extensions (plan:462-463).
recommendation: Add an export acceptance item to WP2/WP6 and to the later slit work: a glue-solar data_exporter that writes the raw FITS/gWCS header of _GlueWCS and converts Time to ISO or MJD. Make the path extraction produce a Data (core PathSlicedData) so it can be saved, exported and restored.

title: The raster cursor readout prints (lat, lon), unlabeled, where IRIS-9 asks for solar (x, y)
verified: The readout on a raster map is '82" 112" (world)': latitude then longitude, unlabeled, in all tiers. This is WCSAxes format_coord following IRIS's WCS world order (wave, HPLT, HPLN). The precision is not fixed at whole arcsec: astropy formats with the current tick spacing (_fl_spacing), so it depends on zoom. Labelling or reordering is a valid low-priority Qt #74/WP1 item.

title: WP4 sync: the raster-map viewer cannot drive time, and offsets are computed but not shown
verified: The WP4 prototype deliberately ignores any source viewer whose x or y axis is a leading (step/scan) axis, so a raster map or stack map viewer never drives SJI time. SJI and spectrogram stepping do sync. The signed offset (-70 ms) is computed by the test, but the prototype shows it nowhere. The plan already requires visible offsets (plan:437, 591-593), so this is a prototype gap against an existing requirement plus an unspecified map-to-frame rule.
recommendation: The WP4 production brief should define how a map's scan maps to an SJI frame (for example scan start or the step under the lock) and show the signed offset in the frame-time readout.

title: Inventory F197 shortcuts: a registry exists but cannot express CRISPEX modifier combos
verified: glue-qt's keyboard_shortcut registry holds only Tab and Backspace, and GlueApplication.keyPressEvent compares event.key() alone. CRISPEX modifier combos (Shift+F/B, Shift+A/S, Ctrl+Shift+I/O) therefore cannot be distinguished. A focused slice slider already steps with the arrow keys. The inventory F197 status cannot be verified because the inventory is not in the plan or the prototypes.
recommendation: Set F197 to exists_needs_preset_or_docs. Document arrow-key stepping (WP9) and, if parity is wanted, register single-key frame and wavelength steps in glue-solar.

title: The SJI time-axis label shows as 'Time (Utc)', not 'Time (UTC)'
verified: Glue displays the SJI time axis as 'Time (Utc)', so the plan and the WP9 doc text 'Time (UTC)' are wrong about what users see. The cause is glue core's axis_label applying .title() to the gWCS name 'Time (UTC)', not the loader. A WP1 name change cannot preserve the capitalisation (tier iii with WP1 also shows 'Time (Utc)'). The fix is either documenting the actual label or an upstream core change.
recommendation: Document the actual label in WP9, or have WP1 preserve 'UTC' capitalisation.
evidence: irispy SJI gWCS world_axis_names printed ('Longitude', 'Latitude', 'Time (UTC)'). .venv glue/core/coordinate_helpers.py:188-189 returns world_axis_names[...].title(). crispex-replay/results_{i,iii}.jsonl step 01 sji_world contains 'Time (Utc)'. plan:368-369, 984.

title: WP4 time linking fails on every negative-step (STEPS_AV<-0.01) raster
verified: For STEPS_AV<-0.01 rasters, irispy flips the data and the times together, so the Time component correctly descends along the flipped step axis. wp4_common.nearest (lines 43-44) rejects an unsorted reference, so link_time (line 62) raises for a single scan and for a 2-scan stack of 3400109360, while a positive-step scan links fine. gwcs_raster_clean also reverses the times, so upgrading irispy does not help. The fix belongs in `nearest`: argsort the reference and map the indices back.
recommendation: In `nearest`, argsort the reference, search in the sorted copy and return the original indices. Keep the NaT/empty checks. WP4 acceptance test: link_time on a 3400109360 scan and a 2-scan stack must not raise, and matched offsets must be under half the cadence.
evidence: My probe (WP1 + released core 1.27.0): neg-scan descending=true, link_time 'ValueError: times must be finite and reference times sorted'; neg-stack same error; pos-scan (4000005156) 'ok'. File order: XCENIX -907.889 to -970.733 and TIME ascending. Code: .venv irispy/io/spectrograph.py:158 (v34) and :259 (times=t_obs[::-1]); `git -C ~/Git/irispy show gwcs_raster_clean:irispy/io/spectrograph.py` :149 times=times[::-1]. Plan line 800 records 'rejects empty, unsorted or NaT references' as the intended behaviour.

title: Masks, 4D-stack NaNs and moments are wrong for negative-step rasters
verified: irispy 0.8.1, v0.9.0 and upstream LM-SAL main (34b5805, 2026-09-21) build the mask from the unflipped data and flip only the data. They also leave per-step meta unflipped (exposure time, FOV centre, OBS_VRIX, OPHASEIX). As a result the per-scan mask, the stack's NaN positions and the WP2 moments are all wrong for negative-step rasters. The error in the moments comes from the mask alone: rerunning line_moments with the mask replaced by data==-200 removes it.
recommendation: Add a version-gated loader workaround (flip the mask when STEPS_AV<-0.01 and irispy lacks the fix), or require a fixed irispy. WP1/WP2 acceptance tests on 3400109360: mask equals data==-200 per scan; stack NaN positions equal the flipped raw -200 values; moments match a numpy reference.
evidence: My probe: irispy cube mask_eq_raw_bad=true, mask_eq_data_bad=false, mismatch=7026; meta fov Tx first=-907.889 while WCS step0 lon=-0.26965 deg (-970.73"). Stack: scan0 nan_valid=3513 and kept_m200=3513; scan1 58509. Moments with loaded vs corrected mask differ in 2987 map pixels: velocity 85.53 km/s, centroid 0.381 A, width 0.193 A, intensity rel 0.0888. Code: spectrograph.py:251,260,271,228-229; `gh api repos/LM-SAL/irispy/contents/irispy/io/spectrograph.py?ref=main` shows the same lines 251/260/271; gwcs_raster_clean:269-270 flips the mask. The plan has no STEPS_AV/V34 mention (grep).

title: irispy's SJI/AIA gWCS is one pixel off the FITS header
verified: irispy's SJI/AIA gWCS passes the 1-based header CRPIX to dkist's VaryingCelestialTransform, which applies Shift(-crpix) to 0-based pixels. Glue's world at 0-based pixel p therefore equals the FITS world at p-1. The error is one image pixel (0.47" for the rolled binned SJI, 0.168" full-res, 0.607" AIA). The WP4 slit column (SLTPX1IX used as a 0-based column) agrees with the raster only because of this shift, so either the overlay column or the world readout will be one pixel off once the WCS is fixed. The plan does not mention this.
recommendation: Report upstream and version-gate a fix. WP1 acceptance test: per-frame corners and centre of a rolled SJI, a deconvolved SJI and an AIA cutout must match an astropy WCS built from CRPIX, CDELT, XCENIX/YCENIX and PCij_IX to within 0.05 px. WP4's slit column currently agrees with the raster (0.005") only through the shifted gWCS; retest slit_x when this is fixed.
evidence: My probe: world at 0-based CRPIX matches XCENIX/YCENIX to 1.4e-10"/6.9e-11"/1.6e-11" (rolled/decon13/aia171), and at CRPIX-1 it is off by 0.4705/0.1682/0.6067". astropy WCS(header) puts CRVAL (111.041, 79.6021") at 0-based CRPIX-1. Code: .venv irispy/io/sji.py:53; dkist 1.18.1 wcs/models.py:97 'shift = m.Shift(-crpix[0]) & m.Shift(-crpix[1])' (also upstream DKISTDC main :97); irispy origin/main sji.py:83 and gwcs_raster_clean sji.py:39. `grep -i crpix` on the plan returns nothing.

title: ROI propagation to a full-resolution SJI takes about 10 s per frame
verified: A raster ROI evaluated on the 32x771x1506 SJI takes about 10 s per full-resolution frame with both link_hpc and WCS autolink. A viewer-sized 600x800 fixed-resolution buffer, which is closer to what an Image Viewer draws, still takes about 4.1 s per frame, too slow for CRISPEX-style slider browsing. I did not re-measure the 338.8 s full-cube link_hpc figure, which was taken while another probe was running. The plan (lines 452-456) already requires recording latency on a larger dataset but sets no budget and has no test.
recommendation: Add a WP1/WP4 performance test on a full-resolution SJI plus raster pair with a per-frame budget. Profile the FITS -TAB world-to-pixel path before choosing link types for the quicklook preset.
evidence: My sequential runs: link_hpc (WP1, released core) s_full_frame_get_mask=10.03, s_frb_600x800=4.09/4.09; autolink (WP1 + core-combined) 9.89, 4.17/4.15; load average about 1.3-1.5. The finder's timing.jsonl shows 338.8/10.4 (link_hpc) and 10.0/9.9 (autolink).

title: The browser hides deconvolved SJIs and can drop the plain file
verified: scan.py:165 (and wp8_scan.py:169) keys SJIs by TDESC1, and deconvolved files carry the same plain TDESC1 ('SJI_2796', 'SJI_2832'). With both variants present, name sorting ('.' < '_') lets the deconvolved file overwrite the plain one. The browser then shows a single 'SJI_2796' entry, which loads the deconvolved cube, and the dataset label (iris.py:125) has no marker. The test tree used two names for the same deconvolved file; that a real plain file also has TDESC1=SJI_2796 is inferred from the plain SJI_1400 header following the same convention.
recommendation: Key and label SJIs with the filename suffix (for example 'SJI_2796 (deconvolved)'). WP8 test: a folder holding both variants lists and loads both, and each label shows which is which.
evidence: My scan_directory run on a tree with both names gave '4000005156 {'SJI_2796': '..._t000_deconvolved.fits.gz'} nfiles 1'. Headers: TDESC1 SJI_2796 and SJI_2832 for the two deconvolved files and SJI_1400 for the plain 4000255147 file; none has a DECON keyword. The WP8 brief (plan 953-971) has no variant handling. IRIS_PLAN_PROTOTYPES/wp9chk/browser-ux.txt:78 records that the download page offers 'SJI fits.gz (+deconvolved)'.

title: Main's wrapper with #2595 suggests a WCS link that then fails
verified: Reproduced: with main's wrapper plus core-combined, a rolled SJI paired with a sunpy make_fitswcs_header map gets 1 suggested autolink. SJI-to-map ROI then raises the latitude-range ValueError, and map-to-SJI selects 0 of 57820 pixels, while WP1's wrapper matches both ways. The finding misstates the plan, though. The table (546-553) makes no claim about SJI/sunpy-map pairs, and lines 554-557 already describe a latitude-range error from main's wrapper, which WP1 fixes. The real gap is that WP1's sunpy-map pairing tests (716-718) do not say to apply the links and check ROI propagation.
recommendation: WP1 acceptance test: apply every suggested autolink and check ROI propagation for a rolled SJI against a sunpy-style map, instead of only counting links.

The finder's grid.jsonl shows wp1-core with 0 mismatches.

title: The WP4 quicklook treats AIA cutouts as SJIs
verified: wp4_common.quicklook:178 does classify any dataset with a 'time' physical type as an SJI, and AIA cutouts have [lon, lat, time]. Their OBSID ('20250519_165924_3640107442') reduces to the IRIS OBSID, so they would be time-linked to a matching raster. That nearest-frame AIA link is arguably useful context rather than a defect. A zero slit only appears if add_slit is applied to an AIA cube: quicklook never calls add_slit, but its guard would not stop it, because irispy's AIACube also carries a (zero) 'slit x position'. An AIA cutout becomes the first image viewer only when no SJI is selected, since the browser picks SJIs before AIA.
recommendation: Classify by INSTRUME or cube class (SJICube vs AIACube). WP4 test: a mixed SJI+AIA+raster selection pairs only the SJI and never adds a slit to AIA.
evidence: Headers: every AIA file in the 3640107442 _SDO folder has SLTPX1IX/SLTPX2IX all zero (357/357 for 171), and TIME ranges from -590.965 to 3681.034 s. My probe gives aia171 physical types [lon, lat, time]. Code: irispy sji.py:210 (adds slit x position for both classes), :239 (AIACube chosen by INSTRUME), wp4_common.py:22-28 (add_slit guard) and 157-166 (observation_key split on '_').

title: F116: multi-exposure rasters make the step inverse ambiguous (not a blocker)
verified: All local rasters with NEXP_PRP>1 are sit-and-stare (4000255147: 1600; 3660259102: 1020), as is the irispy 20210905 fixture (1872). On the synthetic NEXP_PRP=2 raster, times ascend. World-to-pixel returns the first exposure of each position (0, 2, ..., 14), so a step-0 box selects 0 grid pixels and a step-1 box selects 50, while a grid box selects 601 pixels on all 16 steps. I could not locate the 'F116' inventory row in the repo or scratch.
recommendation: Document the degenerate step inverse. Add a WP1 test with a duplicated-position raster checking that grid-to-raster selection covers both exposures.
evidence: My header scan of ~/DATA/IRIS/*_raster gives NEXP_PRP 1 for every scanning raster, and 1600/1020 only for STEPS_AV=0 sit-and-stare. irispy/data/test/{sns,raster}/iris_l2_20210905..._r00000.fits: NEXP_PRP 1872, STEPS_AV 0.0. Rerunning nexp_probe.py (WP1, released core) gives 'world->pixel step ... [0. 2. 4. 6. 8. 10. 12. 14.]', box (-0.5,0.5) -> 0, box (0.5,1.5) -> 50, and grid box -> [601 x16]. `grep -rn F116` finds nothing.
